hints.S26_A1: The bubbles are CATCHING THE LIGHT, exactly as TINY PEARLS do. Ask: which quality does a soap bubble truly share with a pearl - its weight, its roughness, or its milky colour? Match the adjective to what your eye actually sees.
hints.S26_A2: The clue is SOAP AND WATER: you cannot use soap to dry, hide or lotion anything. Ask: which verb means to clean with soap and water? Read every option back into the sentence before you decide.
hints.S26_A3: SLEEP helps the body FIGHT OFF ILLNESSES, so the body is growing stronger, not weaker. Ask: which verb means to regain health and strength? 'Collapse' and 'weaken' point the wrong way entirely.
hints.S26_A4: The dash tells you exactly how she feels: FULL OF ENERGY and READY FOR ANYTHING. Ask: which idiom means feeling wonderful and healthy? 'Under the weather' means ill, and 'a piece of cake' means easy - neither is a feeling of joy.
hints.S26_A5: Omar is to SPEND MORE TIME OUTDOORS instead, so his SCREEN TIME must shrink - though not vanish. Ask: which phrasal verb means to reduce the amount of something? 'Run out' means to finish it completely.
hints.S26_B1: The subject is NOBODY, not 'our class'. Words like nobody and everyone behave like ONE person. Ask: in the present tense, does a singular subject take the plain verb, or the verb ending in -s?
hints.S26_B2: HAS, plus SINCE the beginning of last term: an action that started in the past and still runs today. Ask: after 'has', which form of the verb do we need - the plain verb, the -ing form, or the past participle?
hints.S26_B3: The LUNCH BELL RANG - one sudden moment cutting into something already happening. Ask: which form shows an action still in progress in the past? A plain past verb only reports a finished action.
hints.S26_B4: THAN compares exactly two drinks, so a comparative is needed - and this adjective is irregular. Ask: what does 'good' turn into when two things are compared? 'More good' is never English, and 'best' needs three or above.
hints.S26_B5: WATER cannot be counted: you never say 'one water, two waters'. Ask: which quantity phrase works with an uncountable noun? 'Many', 'several' and 'a few' all count separate items one by one.
hints.S26_B6: EACH means one student at a time, however many sat in the HEALTH TALK. Ask: does a singular subject take a singular verb or a plural one? Check the time too: the LEAFLET reaches them now, not last year.
hints.S26_B7: BY PARENT VOLUNTEERS shows the boxes receive the action, and EVERY DAY shows it happens again and again. Ask: LUNCH BOXES is plural, so which passive helper matches a plural subject in the present tense?
hints.S26_B8: TOLD + somebody + an instruction. Ask: after 'told the students', does English use the plain verb, the -ing form, or the infinitive with 'to'? Reported orders always follow one fixed pattern.
hints.S26_C1: The FIVE SIMPLE HEALTH RULES have only just been mentioned, so they sit right here in front of us - and there is more than one. Ask: which pointing word is plural AND close by? 'Those' would push them far away.
hints.S26_C2: WITHOUT A SINGLE EXCEPTION: the rule covers every person in the class, leaving nobody out. Ask: which word means every single member of a group? 'Some' would cover only a part of it.
hints.S26_C3: This is positive advice: we SHOULD EAT FRUITS AND VEGETABLES, a certain quantity of them, at every meal. Ask: which word gives an unspecified amount in a POSITIVE sentence? Its partner belongs in negatives.
hints.S26_C4: Look at the negative: TRY NOT TO EAT it. Ask: in a negative sentence, which word means 'not even a little'? Its positive partner belongs in blank 3, where the advice says what we SHOULD EAT.
hints.S26_C5: ANOTHER RULE has just been named - one single habit, sitting right here in the sentence. Ask: which pointing word is singular and near? 'These' would need more than one habit; 'that' would push it far away.
hints.S26_C6: The blank stands for a whole group of people, defined by what they do: they EXERCISE REGULARLY. Ask: which pointing word can mean 'the people who...' in front of WHO? A singular word cannot cover a whole group.
hints.S26_C7: Nothing among our BAD HABITS beats STAYING UP LATE - not one of them is HARDER TO BREAK. Ask: which word means 'not one, not any at all'? 'Some' would say the opposite.
hints.S26_C8: After SAID comes a whole reported statement: keeping the FIVE RULES REQUIRES EFFORT. Ask: which word links a reporting verb to the clause it introduces? Here it works as a conjunction, never as a pointing word.
hints.S26_D1: The dash defines it: a VARIETY OF FOODS FROM DIFFERENT FOOD GROUPS, instead of only one. Ask: which box word describes a diet holding every kind of food in the right amounts? 'Nutrients' is a noun; it cannot describe a diet.
hints.S26_D2: The dash tells you exactly what it is: A HOLE IN A TOOTH, made by BACTERIA feeding on leftover food. The blank follows 'a painful', so it names one single thing. Ask: which box word is that hole?
hints.S26_D3: The sentence defines the blank: DRINKING ENOUGH WATER all day, especially after SPORTS. It follows 'Staying', so it must describe you, not name a thing. Ask: which box word means holding enough water inside the body?
hints.S26_D4: The dashes explain it: SITTING AND STANDING UP STRAIGHT, which PROTECTS THE SPINE. The blank follows 'Good', so it names a thing. Ask: which box word means the way you hold your body?
hints.S26_D5: RUNNING OR SKIPPING for THIRTY MINUTES makes the HEART beat hard - this is not gentle exercise. Ask: which box word describes activity demanding a lot of energy? 'Sluggish' means slow and dull, the very opposite.
hints.S26_E1: The word CHILD does not build its plural with -s. Ask: what do you call more than one child? The same trick appears in tooth/teeth and foot/feet: the word changes shape instead of taking an ending.
hints.S26_E2: The WELLBEING belongs to the PUPILS - the sentence is not pointing at a place. Ask: does the underlined spelling mean 'at that spot', or 'belonging to them'? Choose by meaning, never by sound.
hints.S26_E3: The base verb RUN has a short vowel followed by ONE consonant. Ask: what must happen to that final consonant before -ING is added? Compare sit/sitting, swim/swimming and jog/jogging.
hints.S26_E4: Find the real subject: the PUPILS, not the word CLASS that happens to sit beside the blank. Ask: is that subject one, or many? Match the verb to the head noun, never to the nearest noun.
hints.S26_E5: The REPORT belongs to the TWO SCHOOL nurses - two owners, not one. Ask: does a plain -s show ownership, or only make a plural? When the owners are many, does the apostrophe go before the -s, or after it?
hints.S26_F1: IF opens the condition; the second sentence gives the consequence. Ask: which tense belongs inside the IF clause - present or future? A common slip is to push 'will' into both halves, yet it belongs in only one.
hints.S26_F2: 'WOULD RATHER' is not a complete verb on its own - an action must follow it. Ask: what does LENA actually do with fresh fruit? Put that action in its plain base form, then use 'than' before the food she likes less.
